title: On September 9th, a college that started with one man's stubborn idea became a university.
sources: MapsOfIndia - 9th September 1920: The Anglo-Oriental College of Aligarh was converted into the Aligarh Muslim University
caption:
On September 9th, a college that started with one man's stubborn idea became a university.

In 1875, Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College - a bet that Muslims in India needed modern, Western-style education without giving up their own identity. On September 9, 1920, an Act of the legislature converted it into Aligarh Muslim University.

Sir Syed Ahmad Khan didn't live to see the university - he died in 1898. It took the Muslim University Association, founded around 1900, two more decades of fundraising and organizing before the Act finally passed.

Every college, research lab or training institute being built today is making the same bet Sir Syed made - that education built now pays off for a generation that hasn't been born yet.
